note: THE CANDIDATE RECORD'S SHAPE, AND THE TEXT THE MODEL IS SHOWN BEFORE IT
COMPOSES ONE (kogaki#1126).
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. `src/leg-schema.json` declares the shape of ONE
LEG; nothing declared the shape of the CANDIDATE the Legs hang from. So
the Candidate's own fields were carried by `input_shape` -- one sentence
naming keys -- and the one field that reaches the OWNER, the option the
Candidate gate renders, was a single free-prose string. Whether an option
read `Adversarial: the reader is handed ...` or as an unbroken paragraph
was the composing Model's habit on the day, and the Harness guaranteed
neither half.
THE MEASURED SHAPE, at the Candidate gate of
runs/brief/brief-2026-09-15T22-53-48-359Z. Three options rendered with the
whole of the reader experience plus the figure clause in the LABEL and the
bare record id -- `A`, `B`, `C` -- in the description column, because
`composeGateCall` shows an option's id where it carries no description of
its own. The id is a join key between the gate and adoption; it is not
content, and it told the owner nothing.
SO THE MODEL CHOOSES VALUES INSIDE A HARNESS-ENFORCED FORMAT (owner
decision 2026-09-09). The two halves the rendering wanted are two FIELDS --
`characteristic` and `reader_experience` -- and `assembleSelection` renders
them into the option's label and description. A format the Harness composes
from declared fields cannot be a habit that lapses.
IT IS READ TWICE, which is the property `src/leg-schema.json` exists for
and the reason this is a file rather than a longer sentence. The
path-composition state of the Brief workflow table renders it into the
judge's prompt, and `compose_path`'s own validator refuses against the same
field set -- so the text the Model composes against and the text the
refusal enforces are one text and cannot disagree.
THE LEDGER FIELDS ARE HERE FOR THE SAME REASON THE TWO RENDERING
FIELDS ARE (kogaki#1129). `obligations`, `coverage` and `unused` were named
in one prose sentence -- `compose_path`'s `input_shape` -- and in no
declaration, so the composing Model chose their key names and the code that
reads them bound different ones: `raised_at`/`owed`/`settled_at` against
`text`/`introduced_by`/`discharged_by`, `role` against `role_in_thesis`, an
array against an object. Two of the three misreadings were SILENT -- the
Candidate gate rendered every entry as undischarged, and the coverage
section would have said `(not stated by the composer)` of a role the
composer stated -- and the third refused at the Brief's final write, after
two gates and three judge calls, outside every re-ask window. A sentence
describes; a declaration binds, and these three are now declared.
IT DECLARES SHAPE AND MEANING, AND JUDGES NEITHER. A missing field, a blank
one, an over-long characteristic and two Candidates stating the same
characteristic are refused here. Whether the characteristic NAMES the path
well is judgment, and it is judged at path review like every other MUST of
the composition design.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982). The
rule these entries are written under lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here.
THE NAMES THIS FILE USES, and the spec each one names:
The Candidate gate

SPEC-draft-pipeline
what_a_candidate_is: A Candidate is ONE COMPOSED READER PATH: an ordered sequence of Legs
taking the reader from the Brief's Reader start to the adopted Thesis,
plus the reasoning it was composed with. Two or three are composed per
article and they DIFFER IN READER EXPERIENCE -- not in decoration, not in
wording, and not in which Strands they happen to name first.
THE OWNER CHOOSES BETWEEN THEM AT THE CANDIDATE GATE, and that is the one
surface a Candidate has. Two fields below are that surface:
`characteristic` names the path in a few words and `reader_experience`
explains it. Everything else a Candidate carries is read by the runtime.
The Candidate gate is where the count, the difference-in-experience rule
and the premise negation are defined.
the_option_format: THE HARNESS COMPOSES THE OPTION; THE MODEL FILLS ITS FIELDS. Neither half
of the rendering below is composed by the party that writes this record,
and a Candidate cannot change the shape by writing its prose differently.
`<n>` is the option's POSITION in the rendered set, numbered from 1. It is
not the `candidate_id`: the id is the join key the owner's answer resolves
through and it is never shown as content, which is the defect kogaki#1126
closes. The figure clause is the Harness's own sentence about how many
Legs carry a figure; nothing here writes it.
SO THE TWO FIELDS ARE WRITTEN FOR THEIR SEATS. A `characteristic` that is
a sentence does not fit a label, and a `reader_experience` that repeats the
characteristic wastes the only line the owner gets to read.

candidate_id.description: This Candidate's own id, unique within the composed set. It is the JOIN KEY the owner's answer at the Candidate gate resolves through, and it is never rendered to the owner as content -- not as a label, not as a description. Short and mechanical is right here (`A`, `B`, `C`); a value composed to be read is a value in the wrong field.

characteristic.description: A SHORT NAME FOR THIS PATH, in a few words -- `Adversarial`, `Disillusionment first`, `Construction from the substrate up`. It is what the owner scans, so it names the path's character rather than describing its content: no sentence, no trailing clause, no colon introducing an explanation, because the explanation is the next field and rendering both here would leave the description restating the label. Bounded at 48 characters, refused above it -- the bound is the label's seat in the selector rather than a style preference, and a characteristic that needs more than 48 characters is an explanation that has drifted up a field.

reader_experience.description: WHAT THE READER GOES THROUGH on this path, stated so the difference from the sibling Candidates is legible -- this is the axis Candidates differ on, and the difference must be stated to be selectable. It renders as the option's DESCRIPTION, with the figure clause appended by the Harness, so it is written as the explanation of the characteristic above and never as a repeat of it. Two Candidates stating the same reader experience are refused, folded, as are two stating the same characteristic: either the paths do not differ or they are one path presented twice.

legs.description: The ordered Reader Path itself. Every entry is a Leg, whose fields, their meanings and their refusals are declared in `src/leg-schema.json` -- rendered into this same prompt and enforced by `validateLegs`. Nothing about a Leg is restated here.

reasoning.description: The composition-time reasoning this Candidate was composed with, one non-blank string per key. It is the Candidate's gate evidence and the Brief's closing sections are filled from `thesis_closure` and from the tradeoffs at adoption -- adoption fills no default, so a blank value is refused here, inside the re-ask window, rather than at the write.

reader_start.description: Where the reader stands when the path begins. One of the three reader fields the settled structure section names; path composition writes it PER CANDIDATE and adoption fills no default.

reader_target.description: Where the path leaves the reader. The second of the three reader fields, written per Candidate on the same terms.

opening_question.description: The question the article opens on, on this path. The third of the three reader fields, written per Candidate on the same terms.

coverage.type: object keyed by selected Strand id
coverage.description: WHAT EACH SELECTED STRAND DOES IN THE THESIS, on this path. An OBJECT whose KEYS are the Strand ids of the Brief's closed set -- `L1`, `L2` -- and whose value carries `role_in_thesis`, one non-blank string. The Brief's Strand coverage section renders that string beside the Strand's derived placement, so a value under any other key renders as `(not stated by the composer)` beside a Strand the path in fact placed. An absent `coverage` is the empty object and every placed Strand renders unstated; a key naming a Strand outside the closed set is ignored by the render and refused here, because the set closed at mint and a Brief never fetches.

obligations.description: THE LEG HALF OF CLOSURE (kogaki#1151): what each Leg still owes the reader, entered with the Leg that settles it. Every entry is an object carrying `text` (the obligation in the composer's own words, non-blank), `introduced_by` (the `leg_id` of the Leg that raises it) and EXACTLY ONE of `discharged_by` (the `leg_id` of the Leg that keeps the promise) or `conceded_by` (the `leg_id` of the Leg whose prose tells the reader it is left open). All three id fields name a Leg OF THIS CANDIDATE and are refused otherwise. AN ENTRY CARRYING NEITHER, OR BOTH, IS REFUSED, naming the row -- "unresolved" is not a state this ledger can hold. That is exactly why the key names bind: a ledger the runtime cannot read is scored as wholly open and the owner is shown a confident number over a record nothing understood (kogaki#1129). An absent `obligations` is the empty ledger, which is a statement and not an omission.

unused.description: THE DISCLOSURE FOR MATERIAL THIS PATH LEAVES UNPLACED. An OBJECT -- never an array -- whose KEYS are either a selected Strand id (`L2`) or that Strand's Journey material (`L2.journey`), and whose VALUE is the disclosure text: why the path leaves it unused. The claims rule's third move is omit the Leg, revise the path, or leave the Strand unused, never invention, and this field is where the third move is said out loud. An array carries no key to look the disclosure up under, so every unplaced Strand renders the Harness's default sentence and the composer's reason is lost; it is refused here rather than silently dropped. An absent `unused` is the empty object, and an unplaced Strand then discloses in the Harness's own words.

what_is_judged_elsewhere: Nothing here is a lint over a judgment. Whether the characteristic names
the path WELL, whether the reader experience is the one the Legs actually
produce, and whether the three Candidates differ in a way worth choosing
between are judged at path review. A refusal from this file always names a
SHAPE: a field absent, a field blank, a characteristic over its bound, or
two Candidates whose characteristic or reader experience fold to the same
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint -- which is the rule
this paragraph is an instance of.
